subject: Architecture
title: Sagrada Família: Gaudí's Unfinished Masterpiece
description: A short lesson to help you apply Sagrada Família: Gaudí's Unfinished Masterpiece.

hook.text: Sagrada Família in Barcelona has been under construction since 1882 — and it's still not finished.

buildup.text: Antoni Gaudí devoted 43 years to the project. He lived in his workshop for the final year of his life.

discovery.text: Gaudí used no straight lines. Columns branch like trees, and the ceiling mimics a stone forest canopy.

twist.text: Gaudí died in 1926 after being hit by a tram. He was so disheveled that no one recognized him.

climax.text: Computer-aided design is completing what Gaudí could only sketch. Final completion is expected by 2026.

punchline.text: 144 years to build one church. Gaudí said: 'My client is not in a hurry.'

quiz.question: What inspired the interior columns of Sagrada Família?
options: Classical Greek and Roman column orders
Trees branching into a forest canopy

details.summary: Antoni Gaudí's Sagrada Família in Barcelona, begun in 1882 and still under construction, rejects both historical Gothic and modern industrial approaches. Its interior columns branch like trees, supporting vaults that filter light like a forest canopy.
details.whyItMatters: The Sagrada Família reimagines sacred architecture from biological principles rather than historical precedent. Gaudí replaced flying buttresses with tree-like columns.
takeaways: Begun in 1882, still under construction after over 140 years
Columns branch like trees, supporting forest-canopy vaults
Gaudí devoted the last 43 years of his life to this single project

faq.question: When will the Sagrada Família be finished?
faq.answer: Completion is targeted for 2026, the centenary of Gaudí's death, though the date has slipped before. Modern computer modeling and CNC stone-cutting have accelerated construction dramatically compared to the hand-carved early phases. Some decorative elements may take longer.

faq.question: How do the tree-like columns work structurally?
faq.answer: The columns angle inward and branch at calculated points to direct loads efficiently to the foundations — mimicking how trees distribute weight. This eliminates the need for external flying buttresses that Gothic cathedrals require.
